title: Steve Feinberg Issues DOW Memo on AI Classification Pilot
key_facts: Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg issued a memo, dated 5 Oct 2026, calling for a pilot using AI-enabled tools to modernise how the Department of War classifies and declassifies documents and data.

The memo makes the secretary of the Air Force the department's executive agent for the Automated Classification Management Environment (ACME), AI-aided tools developed by the Department of the Air Force.
The executive agent is to roll out a limited automated security classification capability within 180 days.
If the pilot meets its goals, it becomes the department's 'single, digital authoritative reference' for all original classification decisions.
The under secretary for intelligence and security oversees the effort, with support from the chief information officer.
DefenseScoop reported an August Air Force request for information that cited a hard-copy backlog of about 140 million pages and frequent overclassification.
quote_evidence: Outdated procedures for the classification and declassification of documents and data are endangering the DoW's ability to achieve its mission.
If the pilot meets its goals, the capability will become the department's "single, digital authoritative reference" for all original classification decisions.
why_it_matters_hint: The Pentagon wants AI to speed up and correct how it labels secret material, starting with a six-month pilot.
notes: Memo dated 5 Oct, before the 9 Oct window; first public report date not confirmed here. DefenseScoop is the cited upstream outlet for the Air Force details.
